sections.name: File setup (part 1)
sections.title: Triggers, guard and downloads
sections.what: Runs only on the working branch, either manually or when request files change. It downloads cricket match files and loads them into the database, plus sample Formula 1 timing and pit data and football event data from public sources.
sections.why: The header says the agent cannot reach these hosts, so a GitHub runner fetches them. The branch guard stops a rerun after merging into main.
sections.watch_out: Downloads are trusted without checksums, and a missing pit record is written as a note instead of being filled in.

sections.name: File setup (part 2)
sections.title: Build outputs and commit back
sections.what: Builds fixtures and derived tables, adds bowling style data from a public database as a best-effort step, and writes a manifest. It checks that no file is over 50 megabytes, then commits and pushes any changes to the same branch.
sections.why: The header says it commits back only compact, attributed outputs.
sections.watch_out: The push uses the workflow token, so if the branch is protected or changes during the run, the push fails and the outputs wait for the next run.

summary: Data job that downloads open sports data on a GitHub runner, builds small outputs and commits them back to the working branch.
purpose: Give the app real sourced data where the agent's own machine cannot reach the data hosts.
why: The header says the agent cannot reach these hosts, and that raw downloads never enter git. Likely reason for the branch guard: merging into main must not run it again there.
how: 1) Run only on the working branch, manually or when request files change. 2) Set up Node, packages and the test database. 3) Download sources with retries. 4) Load the cricket data into the database. 5) Build fixtures and derived tables. 6) Check no file is over 50 megabytes. 7) Commit and push any changes.
inputs: Request files in data/requests, public data hosts, and the repository code.
outputs: Committed fixtures, derived tables, a manifest, and records of download times and failures.
risks: Public hosts can change format or go offline, and downloads are not checked with checksums. Outputs are pushed straight to a branch.
debug: Read the GET lines in the log to see which download failed. A pit.missing file means no pit data, which is expected. A step-failed status in the bowling styles meta file means that optional step failed. If there is no commit, look for the nothing new line.
